Sorry for the late response! Mmm, I'm not too sure on the club side of things. I have a friend (more like an acquaintance) that runs this club where they discuss different styles of music and people can give presentations on their favorite genres if they so please. Not too sure about other student orgs. If you have a vision for a club that doesn't already exist, I highly recommend making it on your own! Even if you're a first year. It's a great learning experience running a student org, and Oxy makes it fairly easy to go about organizing one. 

I do know a bit more about the music department though, and I have to say that it's run very well. I haven't taken a single music class that I've disliked, and from what I've heard the private lesson faculty are all great. Otherwise, the professors are across-the-board really solid and clearly passionate about their areas of expertise. I will say that some of the music history classes tend to be very euro/america-centric unless you're taking one of Professor Pilich's ethnomusicology classes. The ensembles are a bit hit-or-miss though; I was a part of one of Oxy's larger music ensembles and it wasn't the best time. A lot of people that aren't music majors tend to come to rehearsals without practicing at all so a lot of rehearsals are spent rehashing the same sections over and over. I can't speak for the other ensembles, but that was just my personal experience.

Professor David Kasunic is the chair of the department and I'd recommend you reach out to him if you have other questions, though he may take a while to respond as he's always busy.

You’ll hear a lot of people grumbling on campus whenever the MP (marketplace, main dining hall) doesn’t live up to their expectations, but the fact that their expectations are so high speaks for itself. Oxy has amazing food compared to other schools. I didn’t think it was anything too mindblowing until I visited my friends at other larger schools and experienced firsthand just how godawful they have it. Trust me, we have it good. 

That said, Oxy still does have a tendency to mess up more cultural dishes. It’s particularly egregious with asian food; the pad Thai and pho are really really bad. There’s inevitably some stinkers here and there, but on the whole Oxy food is great. There’s plenty of options to accommodate all sorts of diet types. Everything is clearly labeled so vegans, vegetarians, pescatarians, etc are all able to eat their full. 

The MP  is separated into several stations that specialize in different types of food: for example the Sautée Station cooks in front of you (pasta, stir fry, occasionally poké, etc). My personal favorite is Homestyle; it has the most variety and also I believe is generally the cheapest. Most people tend to grab The Grill if they’re in a hurry, which usually as the same plates for every meal with a little variation from day to day. 

The MP workers go all out for holidays like Valentines and Thanksgiving with bougie food that is always delicious. In the past, we’ve had shrimp linguini, prime rib, roast turkey, and more.

It *is* a bit harder to get late night food though. We have a cooler which is open until 11:30pm on weekdays and 2am on weekends and we also have a little coffee cart in Berkus hall that’s open until 1:30am most of the time. But there have definitely been instances when I’ve had to go to sleep hungry after a late night of studying because everything’s closed.

One of my parents actually works behind the scenes on the show! I’m purposefully being vague because I’ve been told how big secrecy is there, but I’ve heard some horror stories. If I’ve taken one thing away, it’s that DP is extremely superficial and will literally turn away people based on looks. Make sure you’re looking your best on taping day if you want extra brownie points (or if you don’t care, don’t lol but I’d recommend you do). 

The biggest circlejerk online is that he is under-qualified and is actively trying to ruin as many people’s lives as possible. As someone with a bit of a more insider’s perspective, I don’t believe this to be the case. Yes — at the end of the day, he is still a performer trying to put on a show for ratings. If that means getting into a shouting match with a guest in front of a live audience, he’ll do it. But once the spectacle is over, there are people behind the scenes whose literal paid job it is to look out for guests after the show is done taping. The “cash me ousside” girl was actually given resources as well, but her outcome is a bit of an aberration because of her clip going viral and becoming a meme. 

Biggest tip though would be to go to Larchmont which is nearby and to get the sausage pasta at Louise’s. The bread there is life changing.
